task: Revise W1-30's settlement-33 case (r14) under DEC-757 item 3 so that it holds the ticket's own side, update W1-30's README to match, and check the W1-30 and W2-01 probe-gate suites read-only for any other case DEC-757 item 3 or W2-53's KPI lines 1–4 reverse.
status: DONE — revision committed (`49e4aca0`), the r14 file passes 13/13, and the read-only check found one conditional case, named as package P-A below.
work_completed: The case changed in three ways. (1) Its commit is now the engineer's (`Role: engineer`, `Task: PROJ-prlc`, made with `exact=True`), changes only `.tickets/PROJ-prlc.md` after the probe, and is still refused with the commit and path named. (2) It is renamed from `test_a_commit_of_the_ticket_after_the_probed_one_that_changes_its_ticket_file_refuses` to `test_a_commit_of_the_tickets_own_side_after_the_probed_one_that_changes_its_ticket_file_refuses`. Under DEC-757 an orchestrator's or owner's commit of the ticket that changes only that file no longer refuses, so the old name read as a universal claim is false. (3) The shared guard `_of_the_ticket` can no longer be used here. It requires "W1-50 finds nothing", but W1-50 always flags a worker's commit of a ticket file ("a ticket file in a commit with a worker's Role trailer or made in a worker's call"). Inside this one case it is replaced by explicit checks: the commit names the ticket, it follows the probe, and W1-50 gives exactly one finding, for this commit and the ticket file. `_refused_for` then reads the probe gate's finding among the refusal's parts, so that assertion and the others are kept. I first tried `support.engineer_commit` without `exact=True`, but it hands waiting ticket files to a separate orchestrator commit, so the engineer's commit changed nothing. In the README I updated the round-14 row, the settlement-33 paragraph (quoting DEC-757 item 3: integration side settled, case now holds the own side, renamed, W1-50 note), package P-1 (a "Settled" line) and settlement-list item 33.
files_changed: tests/acceptance/W1-30/test_w1_30_r14_probe_later_commits.py; tests/acceptance/W1-30/README.md
evidence: `printenv GOV_ROLE GOV_TICKET` → `independent-test-designer`, `DAEO-7rr2`. `git rev-parse --show-toplevel --abbrev-ref HEAD` → `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-53`, `w2/W2-53`. DEC-732: `PYTHONPATH=/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-53/src python3 -c "import gov; print(gov.__file__)"` → `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-53/src/gov/__init__.py`. The hooks folder `/home/usain/Dynamic-Agentic-Engineering-OS/.git/hooks` held only `*.sample` files (no `pre-commit`). The commit is `49e4aca0`, "W1-30 settlement 33 under DEC-757 item 3: the ticket-file edit after the probe is the ticket's own side's (W2-53)", 2 files changed, 36 insertions, 7 deletions, with trailers `Task: DAEO-7rr2`, `Role: independent-test-designer`, `Implements: DEC-757`, `Rewrite-Reason: DEC-757 item 3 makes an orchestrator's or owner's commit naming the ticket and changing only its ticket file no change to the probed code; the case now holds the ticket's own side, which still refuses` and `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. `git log --oneline -2` → `49e4aca0 W1-30 settlement 33 under DEC-757 item 3: …`, `a10a9eb3 W2-53 (DAEO-7rr2): acceptance tests, red`. `git status --short` → empty.
tests: `PATH=/home/usain/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.3/bin:$PATH PYTHONPATH=/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-53/src python3 -m pytest tests/acceptance/W1-30/test_w1_30_r14_probe_later_commits.py -q -p no:cacheprovider -rs` → 13 passed in 26.71 s, none skipped, none failed. The revised case passes today: today's code refuses the engineer's ticket-file edit after the probe.
discoveries: (1) W1-50 always flags a worker's commit of a ticket file, so a ticket-file-only own-side commit that names the ticket can never make the probe gate the only gate with a finding. Every such case has to read the probe gate's finding among the refusal's parts, as W2-53's own-side cases do. (2) In W2-53's README, P-2 and the line "W1-30's probe tests are touched too" still use the case's old name. (3) Check result: W2-01's probe suites (`test_w2_01_probe_merge_back.py`, `test_w2_01_probe_rounds.py`; the other W2-01 files contain no probe-gate cases) and W1-30's `test_w1_30_probe.py`, `_probe_commits.py`, `_r8_probe_record.py`, `_r10_probe_records.py`, `_r13_probe_findings.py`, `_r8_commits.py`, `_r14` and `_r13_probe_merge.py` hold no other case that DEC-757 item 3 reverses. Against KPIs 1–4, every refusing merge case either differs from git's own merge (an edit, a removal, `ours`) or has a conflict, so it is judged against the probed code. The merge cases that close are git's own merges. The r8 and r13 cases whose wanted refusal may name either the later commit or the merge still stand. The one conditional case is package P-A.
risks: (1) I followed "touch no other line of W1-30's suite", so the r14 module docstring (lines 20–21, "the ticket's own ticket file … a commit of the ticket after the probed one that changes it refuses, as today") is now stale: it does not mention DEC-757's integration-side exception. (2) The revised case pins W1-50's current single finding (commit and paths). If W1-50 later changes what it reports for a worker's ticket-file commit, this guard fails as "the fixture is wrong" even though the probe gate behaves correctly.
lessons: (1) `Project.commit` without `exact=True` moves waiting ticket files into a separate orchestrator commit, so a worker's ticket-file edit needs `exact=True`. (2) The `_of_the_ticket` guard in r14 cannot hold for any worker's ticket-file commit.
proposed_decisions: P-A — W1-30 r13 `test_a_merge_of_a_later_head_that_changed_only_tests_refuses` (`test_w1_30_r13_probe_merge.py`) against KPI 4 (and KPI 1).
- **Question:** Must the refusal still name the merge-back of a later head whose only later change is a designer's acceptance test, when that merge is git's own merge of its parents?
- **Why now:** The case passes only if the refusal names `merge`. Under W2-53 the merge's probed paths are exactly what git's own merge gives, so KPI 1 does not refuse it, and KPI 4 read literally ("a merge whose probed paths are what git's own merge of its parents gives … pass[es]") lets it pass. The close is still refused, by rule 3 of DEC-581, but for the designer's commit. If the engineer drops settlement 24's "the head merged is the probed commit" condition, this case goes red even though the behaviour is correct.
- **Options:**
  - (a) Keep settlement 24's condition alongside the git-merge measure, so the merge is still named; no test change.
  - (b) A fresh W1-30 test designer revises the case so that the refusal may name either the designer's commit or the merge (as the sibling `…changed_the_code_refuses` already does), with `Rewrite-Reason:` naming KPI 4.
  - (c) Leave it and decide when the engineer's run shows it.
- **Impact:** (a) keeps two merge rules in the gate. (b) changes one assertion; the refusal itself stays.
- **Reversibility:** Full.
- **Cost:** (a) small in the gate; (b) one line in one case.
- **Recommendation:** (b), made only if the engineer's W1-30 run shows it red.
- **Confidence:** medium.
unresolved: (1) The stale r14 module docstring lines 20–21. (2) The old case name in W2-53's README (P-2 and the W1-30 line), which is not mine to change. (3) Whether P-A turns red depends on the engineer's implementation.
recommended_next_action: The orchestrator commits DEC-757 to the register, hands W2-53 to the engineer with W1-30's suite in the run (watching P-A), and has W2-53's designer point README P-2 at the renamed case.
